USER_STORY: As a user importing a foreign-currency statement twice, I want the transfer rows caught as duplicates like the expenses are, so a second import does not move the money twice.

At a rate of 58 only the expense is flagged (through original_amount); the transfer row is selected for import ("Import 1 row" covers it) and would post a second transfer of ₱5,800.00. src/lib/importDuplicates.ts `matchDuplicates` files every movement (isMovement) only under `transferKey`, keyed on the converted amount, and never under `originals`, although the stored transfer has original_amount 100.00 USD. SUMMARY: Editing a row into a transfer to a card records no card payment
USER_STORY: As a user who fixes a mis-recorded card payment, I want the edit to log the payment like a new one would, so the card's payment history and statement agree with its balance.
DESCRIPTION: Found by LED-208 (knowledge/retros/2026-10-02-live-sweep-sheet-edits-offline.md). Observed at 390, demo user: "Visa payment" (a 700.00 transfer to Visa Platinum with its credit_card_payments row) edited Kind Transfer → Expense removes the payment row and reverts the card's last payment, correctly (LED-191 trigger). Edited back, Kind Expense → Transfer, To account Visa Platinum: the balances return (Visa −1,528.74, checking unchanged) but no credit_card_payments row is created, and the card's last payment stays 650.00 on 2026-08-10. Every create path runs the statement steps for a transfer into a card (useCardPayment.createWithStatement for the Card payment kind and a plain Transfer, recordGenerated for recurring rows, recordSynced for a queued one); the update path does not, and the LED-191 trigger in supabase/migrations/20261001100000_card_payment_follows_its_transfer.sql only updates or deletes a linked row. The same gap applies when an existing transfer's destination is moved onto a card. Suggested fix: on update, when the row becomes a transfer into a card and has no linked payment, run the same statement steps as a create (client path through useCardPayment, or an insert branch in the trigger with the statement update kept client-side); cover a queued edit too.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Expense → Transfer to a card creates one linked payment row and updates the card's last payment and statement as a new payment does; (b) moving a transfer's destination from savings to a card does the same, and from a card to savings removes it; (c) a queued edit gets the same result on drain; (d) balances unchanged from today's behaviour; (e) re-run the LED-208 kind-switch check.

SUMMARY: Recurring rows are posted again by every browser that has not posted them
USER_STORY: As a user who opens Ledger on more than one device or browser, I want each recurring transaction posted once, so a second device does not add the rent or a card payment again.
DESCRIPTION: Found while validating epic 20 (knowledge/retros/2026-10-03-epic-20-phase-4-findings.md). Observed: demo user, seeded monthly "Gym membership" (is_recurring, last row 2026-09-03). Three fresh Playwright browser contexts signed in as the same user on 2026-10-03 each posted a 2026-10-03 "Gym membership" row (created_at 00:07:37, 00:08:23, 00:08:40), so the month held three. generateDueRecurring (src/hooks/useTransactions.ts:387) reads every is_recurring row, and skips a due date only when wasRecurringGenerated(tx.id, nextDate) is true; that marker lives in localStorage (`ledger-recurring-generated`, useTransactions.helpers.ts:130). Another browser, another device, a private window or cleared site data has no marker, so it posts the row again. Each posted row is itself is_recurring with the same interval, and the series parent is not changed, so the copies also post their own next dates. A recurring transfer into a card runs the statement steps once per copy (LED-190). Suggested fix: make the database the record of what was posted, e.g. a unique key on (series, date) with the generated row carrying its series id, or a generation RPC that inserts with on conflict do nothing; keep the localStorage marker only as a shortcut.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Two browsers signed in as the same user, opened on a day a recurring row is due, post it once; (b) a private window or cleared storage posts nothing already posted; (c) a recurring transfer into a card records one payment and one statement step; (d) a migration applies to an empty database, and existing duplicates are left for the user (not deleted silently); (e) re-run the two-context check from the epic 20 retro.
